SOURCE: board DM msg 651 (human:forrest, 2026-09-10T20:26Z): 'I think we need git worktree observability in the chat UI. Maybe Jonah can come up with a good look for feel for this.' Filed by the CTO on the board member's behalf. UX owner: agent:ux-jonah.

WHY NOW: the WIP limit went 1 -> 3 today (#board msg 642). Up to three tasks now run in parallel lanes, each in its own worktree under .worktrees/AS-<n> with its own employee, and none of that is visible from the chat app. The only views are 'git worktree list' and 'lattice branch-link', and both need a shell on the host. The board's stated interface with the company is the chat app; once AS-95 lands and one message drives a whole loop of ticks, the lanes are the thing the board most needs to see and cannot.

WHAT (v1, plausible scope -- the plan refines it): a READ-ONLY view of every linked worktree, one row each: path; branch; linked task (join key AS-<n> from the branch name / lattice branch-link, deep-linked the way AS-93 links task ids); commits ahead of master; dirty or clean; last commit author (employee id, per the git identity convention) and age; and a STALE flag when the worktree still exists but its task is done or cancelled (or the branch is already merged). Derived, never hand-maintained: fed from 'git worktree list --porcelain' plus 'git log master..<branch>' / 'git status --porcelain' per worktree, joined to .lattice/ read-only -- the same doctrine as the derived org chart (AS-33) and the Lattice deep links (AS-93). Explicitly NOT in v1: any write action (no remove-worktree, no merge, no status transition from the UI).

TWO-STAGE PLANNING: (1) Jonah's UX pass -- user flows, screen inventory, state spec (empty / one lane / three lanes / stale / unknown-task), and a low-fi static wireframe under docs/design/ in the AS-30 mould; it is the first half of in_planning. (2) The CTO's technical plan is the second half and consumes the wireframe. Then the normal implement / review lifecycle.

PLANNING QUESTION (decided in the plan, NOT here): the chat server runs in a container and cannot run git against the host repo today. Two candidate feeds: (a) the host watcher writes a worktrees snapshot JSON next to deploy-state.json (apps/chat/data/) on each tick / on a short interval, and the server renders that -- same pattern the deploy line already uses; (b) a read-only mount of the host checkout into the container and git run inside it. (a) keeps git off the container and reuses an existing pipe but is only as fresh as the watcher; (b) is live but adds git to the image and mounts the whole repo. The plan chooses, states the freshness guarantee, and names the falsifier for it (M4).

ORDERING: in the critical Chat set (title prefix 'Chat:', tag chat). Position within the set is the CTO's call (board delegation DM msg 614) and is recorded in a comment on this task and in CLAUDE.md section 'Scheduling priority' by the metawork layer.
data.title: Chat: git worktree observability in the chat UI

data.body: ORDERING (CTO call, delegated by the board in DM msg 614): AS-99 sits THIRD in the Chat set -- after AS-94 and AS-95, ahead of the age queue. Why: (1) the board asked for it directly (DM msg 651); (2) its value scales with the number of parallel lanes, and AS-95 is what makes lanes run unattended -- shipping the view right behind the loop means the board sees the lanes the loop runs from the first loop, not after sixteen more tasks; (3) it displaces nothing that is running: AS-94 and AS-95 keep their lanes, and Jonah's half of planning takes the lane AS-94 frees when it leaves review for needs_human. Proposed CLAUDE.md wording (metawork layer applies): 'AS-99 (Chat: git worktree observability) goes third, after AS-94 and AS-95 and ahead of the age queue -- board DM msg 651, 2026-09-10; CTO ordering call recorded on AS-99.' NOT STARTED THIS TICK: WIP is 3 with AS-94 in review and AS-95 in implementation; Jonah (agent:ux-jonah) starts in_planning (UX half) in the next tick with a free lane. Board pre-input welcome on the host-feed vs mounted-checkout question in the description; default if no preference arrives: the plan decides.

NORTH STAR (board DM msg 658, human:forrest, 2026-09-10T20:36Z, recorded so the planning stage reads it before opening a file): 'The big idea long term, is to have a sort of foreman of the factory view, perhaps even an anthropomorphic view of work in progress. full visualization, like a simulator video game. for this we need to put as much in place as possible to get observability.' Standing operating instruction from the same message: put as much observability in place as possible.

HOW THIS SHAPES AS-99 (CTO ruling, binding on both halves of planning):

1. Reframe the unit from 'worktree' to 'lane'. A worktree is where a lane lives, not what a lane is. One row/card = one lane = {task (AS-n, deep-linked per AS-93), stage (from .lattice status), employee (assignee; last commit author as the git-side confirmation), worktree path + branch, commits ahead of master, dirty/clean, last commit age, STALE flag when the worktree outlives its task}. The tick lock (apps/chat/data/advance.lock: pid, startedAt, source, nonce) is the only liveness signal we have today and is shown at whole-tick granularity, honestly labelled as such -- do not fake per-lane liveness from it.

2. Design the lane card as the component that grows into the floor. Jonah: the UX half specifies the lane card's states (empty / one lane / three lanes / stale / unknown-task / lane-with-no-worktree-yet, i.e. in_planning before the branch is cut) AND leaves an explicit slot for signals that do not exist yet: stage timer, sub-agent alive/exited, current activity. Wireframe those as visibly-absent placeholders ('no live signal yet'), not as invented data. The foreman floor is a later spatial arrangement of the same cards over the same data; it is not a separate app.

3. Feed doctrine: one projection, many views. Whichever feed the technical plan picks (snapshot JSON written by the host watcher beside deploy-state.json -- my lean -- or a read-only mount), the JSON the server renders is a PROJECTION with a named schema (lanes[] with the fields in item 1, plus generatedAt and source), and the plan states its freshness guarantee with an M4 falsifier. AS-100 (filed today) later replaces the snapshot's source with a structured company-events stream; the lane view must not need a rewrite when that happens -- the projection shape is the contract, the producer is swappable.

4. Explicitly OUT of AS-99 v1, deliberately: any write action from the UI; per-tool activity of a running employee (we do not own the harness); animation or spatial layout; token/cost per stage (no source yet); sub-agent spawn/exit events (that is AS-100's job, and it is not started before AS-95 lands).

5. Ordering unchanged: third in the Chat set after AS-94 (needs_human, board bootstrap) and AS-95 (in_progress). AS-100 goes fourth, directly behind this task, because it is the producer this view's second version consumes.

BOARD RULING (DM msg 668, human:forrest, 2026-09-11T01:56Z) on the msg-663 question: BOTH. Employee figures reflect stage-level state (persisted -- AS-100) AND tool-level activity (live only, never persisted -- AS-103, filed the same night). The full two-signal rule is recorded on AS-100.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE UX HALF OF THIS PLANNING STAGE (Jonah): the lane card has TWO LAYERS with different truth rules.
- DURABLE layer: task, stage, employee, worktree/branch, ahead/dirty, last commit age, stale flag -- and once AS-100 lands, stage started-at / elapsed / sub-agent alive. Survives a reload. Every value has a source on disk.
- TRANSIENT layer: a one-line "now:" status at tool granularity ("now: reading server.js", "now: running tests", "now: waiting on docker") fed by live push frames only. It has a DECAY state (goes quiet after N seconds without a frame -- pick N in the spec and say why) and a BLANK-AFTER-RELOAD state (empty until the next frame arrives). It is never shown as history, never scrollable, never counted.
The states ledger must name both transient states explicitly and must not imply the "now:" line can be scrolled back, or that its absence means the employee is idle -- absence means "no live signal", which the durable layer disambiguates. The card's shape does not change across AS-99 -> AS-100 -> AS-103: fields are added, nothing is redrawn.

The technical half of this plan (mine) still decides the feed question in the description ((a) watcher-written snapshot vs (b) read-only mount); the ruling does not touch it.

PLANNING STARTED (orchestrator cto-owen, headless tick watcher:17217:15f8e5d5699f9cba, 2026-09-11 02:43Z), on the board's 'we can continue on with other stuff for now' (DM msg 676). Lane 2 of this tick. First half: Jonah's UX pass (flows, screen inventory, states ledger with the two-layer card from the msg-668 ruling, low-fi wireframe under docs/design/ in the AS-30 mould). Second half, the technical plan (feed choice (a)/(b), projection schema, freshness falsifier), follows in the next tick with a free lane — it consumes the wireframe and must not start before it exists. Planning artifacts commit to master as planning-stage output; the branch and worktree are cut when the plan is complete.

UX half of planning done (agent:ux-jonah). Four artifacts under docs/design/chat-lanes/: 00-flows.md (board, from chat app desktop+phone/tailnet; 4 flows: glance/drill-in/watch-live/return-after-reload; entry point = sidebar 'Lanes' button); 01-screens.md (placement + lane card field list/order + whole-tick liveness line + visibly-absent placeholder slots); 02-states-ledger.md (11 states incl. snapshot-missing, snapshot-stale, transient-decayed, transient-blank-after-reload, mobile-narrow); lanes.html+lanes.css (one composite wireframe: 3 lanes, 1 stale, one now-line variant per lane, reusing wireframes/wireframe.css + tokens.css, zero JS). Plan file has a 'UX half' section pointing at all four plus open questions for the technical half.

PLACEMENT CALL: dedicated 'Lanes' pane opened from a sidebar button (same affordance as the existing 'Org chart' button), not an inline sidebar section -- the durable card (8 fields + 2 placeholder slots) plus the board-ruling's second transient line don't fit the rail without truncating fields, which is exactly the guessed-value failure this task exists to prevent. Also matches NORTH STAR item 2 directly: the card is the seed of the foreman floor, and a future spatial canvas needs a canvas, not a sidebar slot. A passive lane-count badge stays in the sidebar for the ambient glance (Flow 1).

DECAY N = 15s for the now: line, chosen because AS-103's hook-based source can legitimately go quiet for tens of seconds mid-tool-call without the employee stopping; stated as a UX default the technical/AS-103 plan may retune, not a measured constant.

OPEN QUESTIONS for the technical half (also in the plan file): (1) confirm the projection carries generatedAt directly rather than the UI inferring age from file mtime; (2) how employee is sourced when Lattice assignee and last-commit git author disagree -- wireframe shows both; (3) whether unknown-task worktrees actually surface a usable branch name via git worktree list --porcelain for the no-join fallback; (4) whether lane-with-no-worktree-yet needs a second .lattice-sourced input merged into the same projection, since a worktree-only feed has no row for a task before its branch is cut; (5) confirm AS-103 frames are strictly fire-once/ephemeral with no server-side buffering, or blank-after-reload needs a backlog variant.

LEFT OUT FOR TIME: no full-ledger-coverage wireframe (lanes.html draws only the one composite state the task brief asked for; the other 8 ledger rows are spec'd in 02-states-ledger.md but not drawn) -- next pass can add EMPTY/ONE/SNAPSHOT-MISSING renders if the technical plan or implementation wants them. No sidebar badge/button wiring -- that's implementation, not this planning half.

TECHNICAL HALF WRITTEN (cto-owen). FEED: (a) watcher-written git snapshot apps/chat/data/worktrees.json, joined server-side to .lattice/tasks into a lanes projection served at GET /api/lanes and pushed as SSE 'event: lanes'. Why not (b): node:24-slim has no git; every .worktrees/AS-n/.git is a file pointing at an absolute HOST gitdir path that cannot resolve at /repo (so a mount needs the host's exact path + safe.directory + git in the image); the AS-26 file gate makes .git unreachable by design and the container must never gain repo write access; and deploy-state.json / advance-loop.json / advance-watcher.pid are three precedents for exactly this pipe. Join is server-side so stage/assignee stay live and AS-100 later joins as a third input to the same composer (no rewrite). FRESHNESS (M4): snapshot written every lanes poll (15 s, ADVANCE_LANES_POLL_S) with generatedAt; server flags stale past LANES_STALE_MS=60 s; falsifier = planted file with fresh mtime and 61 s-old generatedAt reads stale, 59 s does not. Watcher down => stale in 60 s, never a frozen list shown as current; file absent => 'Lane data unavailable'. JONAH'S QUESTIONS: (1) yes, generatedAt is in the snapshot and the projection; the UI never reads mtime. (2) both fields, never merged: employee.assignee + employee.lastCommitAuthor + agree true/false/null; UI shows both when they differ. (3) yes: porcelain always gives path + HEAD and either a branch or 'detached', so unknown-task cards render with branch/path and are never filtered. (4) yes, a second .lattice-sourced input in the same composer: lanes = non-main worktrees UNION MID_LIFECYCLE tasks with no worktree (the watcher's own constant); git fields read 'not cut yet', never 0/clean. (5) confirmed strictly ephemeral: the SSE fan-out is write-through with no Last-Event-ID and no buffer; recorded as a constraint on AS-103. ALSO: badge shows a count ('Lanes · 2'), no denominator (the WIP limit is prose, not data); 'Lanes · –' when the snapshot is missing. 14 acceptance criteria, each with a mutant and predicted red set; counted run is compose --build with the Image Built receipt, all new tests are node:test and runnable on the host in a headless tick (labelled as such; the receipt run is a live-session merge precondition). Implementer developer-marcus (the watcher factories are his mould); QA suggestion qa-ruben (concurrency seams). Branch feat/AS-99-lane-view, worktree .worktrees/AS-99.

Orchestrator note (tick watcher:76266): the planned transition printed 'run lattice plan-review AS-99 (plan_review_mode: single) before moving to in_progress'. That is Lattice tooling, not the company review gate — the next tick's orchestrator runs or bypasses it per the CLI's own rules before spawning Marcus; do not mistake it for a needs_human.

IMPLEMENTATION STARTED (orchestrator cto-owen, loop tick 2, watcher:76266). Marcus implements the T5 table in .worktrees/AS-99 on feat/AS-99-lane-view. The 'run lattice plan-review' line printed at the planned transition did not gate in_progress — the CLI let the transition through — so it is recorded as advisory tooling output, nothing more. Headless-tick constraints stated in the tasking: commit at logical boundaries because the 30-min tick clock may cut the stage (the lane resumes from the branch next tick); host 'node --test' runs are labelled as such, the counted --build compose receipt waits for a tick or session with docker (AS-92). Board writes stay with the orchestrator.

IMPLEMENTATION CONTINUED (orchestrator cto-owen, loop tick 3, watcher:76266). Last tick's clock cut Marcus after three branch commits (c9c35cc lanes composer + watcher git snapshot primitives; f221372 makeLanesOps tests; 7f6d66b /api/lanes + change-only lanes frames) with the api.test.js additions still uncommitted in the worktree. Marcus resumes in .worktrees/AS-99 from the branch: finish the API tests, then stream frames, public/lanes.js, the pane markup, READMEs, per the T5 table. Same headless constraints as tick 2 (host node --test labelled as such; compose --build receipt is a merge precondition from a session with docker). Board writes stay with the orchestrator.

IMPLEMENTATION CONTINUED (orchestrator cto-owen, loop tick 5, watcher:76266). Tick 3's clock cut Marcus after six branch commits (through 1f7972a, the AC-12 change-only push proof) with the two README sections (apps/chat/README.md 'Lanes pane', watch/README.md worktrees.json row) still uncommitted in the worktree. Marcus resumes from the branch: commit the README work, run the full host node --test suite (labelled as host runs), walk the plan's T5 table and acceptance criteria for anything not yet delivered, run the plan's mutants where a host run can, and report what is done vs. what waits for a docker session. If the table is complete, this stage ends with the task moving to review.

IMPLEMENTATION DONE (agent:developer-marcus, loop tick 5 / watcher:76266), posted by the orchestrator from his report. Two commits this tick: d6c7cc8 documents the lanes feed in both READMEs (last T5 row; every claim checked against the code — poll 15 s, LANES_STALE_MS 60 s, LANES_POLL_MS 5 s, join order, badge dash); 971d6a1 closes AC-3's second half. Branch feat/AS-99-lane-view is 8 commits ahead of master, 15 files, +2360/-13, worktree clean. FINDINGS FIRST: (1) AC-3 was half-implemented and mutation found it — a git runner that throws (EMFILE, cwd vanished under a removed worktree) unwound into evaluate()'s outer catch, and replacing that catch with a rethrow left all tests green at the intended site (advance-watcher.mjs:1685, single match, re-read). Closed with watcher-lanes-never-rejects and -midway (the latter proves a half-built worktrees array degrades to the error shape instead of emitting a truncated lane set as complete). (2) One survivor was the mutation's fault: M11b v1 swapped the clock for mtime instead of the age source; v2 substitutes generatedAt with mtime and goes red — second instance of the AS-95 wrong-mutation hazard, new shape: a unique correct site that still did not express the defect. (3) Cosmetic, left for QA: a per-row git throw is labelled worktree-list-failed by the outer catch; T4's enum closes that label so widening it would be a plan deviation. (4) Probed past the list: data/ is gitignored so worktrees.json cannot dirty the tree and trip the AS-75 refusal; IMAGE_INPUTS already covers lib/public/watch/test/server.js so the merge redeploys unattended; deploy-shape test, compose.yaml, Dockerfile untouched. T5 table: every row delivered (watcher primitives + lanes poll wiring, lib/lattice.js listTasks/idsByShortId, lib/lanes.js composeLanes, server /api/lanes + change-only lanes frames + /lanes.js static, public/lanes.js wording module, index.html pane markup, app.js state/SSE/Escape chain with lanes ahead of org, style.css z-index 37, READMEs, five test files). ACs: 14 of 14 with observed reds — 17 mutants, 17 red, 0 survivors, each site-asserted and re-read on a scratch copy under scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/mut99 (driver run.mjs, results.json); failing sets recorded per mutant, wider sets (AC-1, AC-6, AC-7a, AC-10, AC-11a) are downstream couplings. HOST run: node --test --test-reporter=spec in the worktree's apps/chat: 416 tests, 416 pass, 0 fail (master baseline 367, +49). OWED: the counted docker compose run --rm --build test receipt (no docker in a headless tick, AS-92) — plan T6 makes it a merge precondition, so done waits for a docker session; plan T6's M6 probes (phone-width field count, kill the watcher and watch the caption go stale at ~60 s, throwaway detached worktree shows an unknown-task card, Escape ordering with both modals open) need a running container and live host. Marcus recommends review.

REVIEW STAGE QUEUED (orchestrator cto-owen). Next tick runs the fresh-context QA review against git diff master...feat/AS-99-lane-view inside .worktrees/AS-99 — Ruben by preference (concurrency and the watcher/server seam are his strengths; Priya takes AS-28 in the same tick), findings first and sweep second (M5), M6 probing budgeted. Known gaps for the tasking: the compose --build receipt is outstanding and blocks done (needs a docker session — a headless tick cannot produce it); the T6 live probes need a running container. The reviewer must not read .lattice/review_state/ or any auto-review output before forming findings, and must not read Marcus's scratchpad (mut99) — per-actor scratchpads, M3. AS-100 stays parked at planned until this merges.

REVIEW STARTED (orchestrator cto-owen, loop tick 6 / watcher:76266). Fresh-context QA: agent:qa-ruben, inside .worktrees/AS-99 against git diff master...feat/AS-99-lane-view (8 commits, 971d6a1). Findings first, sweep second (M5), M6 probes budgeted; reviewer told not to read .lattice/review_state/ or any other actor's scratchpad. Headless tick: the compose --build receipt is expected to remain owed unless docker answers by absolute path; a pass without the receipt holds at review, not done. Priya reviews AS-28 in the parallel lane.

VERDICT: implementation-level rework needed (one blocking defect, one non-blocking defect, both small; plan is sound). Reviewed cold by qa-ruben: plan T1-T7 + Jonah's docs/design/chat-lanes, then git diff master...feat/AS-99-lane-view (8 commits, 15 files, +2360/-13). Implementer comments and .lattice/review_state NOT read before these findings were formed.

FINDINGS (outside the criteria list: 2 defects, 3 observations)
F1 DEFECT, BLOCKS (AC-14 spirit / Jonah Flow 1a): on snapshot.reason='git-error' the badge reads 'Lanes · 0' and the pane's empty state reads 'No lanes in flight.' Repro (node, worktree apps/chat): composeLanes({snapshot:{generatedAt:<now-5s>,error:'no-git',worktrees:[]},tasks:[one in_progress task],ids:{},nowMs}) -> {count:0,lanes:[],reason:'git-error'}; describeLanes(...) -> badge 'Lanes · 0'; app.js renderLanes picks 'No lanes in flight.' because view.badge === 'Lanes · 0'. The caption does say git refused, but the badge and the empty-state sentence both assert a measurement when nothing was measured — exactly the 'nothing running' vs 'cannot see' confusion Flow 1a and AC-14 exist to prevent, and the one case a board member glancing at the sidebar would misread. Fix shape: describeLanes returns the dash + 'Lane data unavailable — <git-error sentence>' when reason==='git-error' (lanes may stay [] per T4); renderLanes keys the empty-state sentence off the reason, not the badge string; add a lanes-label test (null-is-dash pattern) and an api test for the git-error badge. Not fixed inline: it is a behaviour change across two files plus tests, not trivia, and I do not review my own work.
F2 DEFECT, non-blocking alone (T4 'absolute host path is not written into the snapshot'): relPathOf(repoRoot, path) returns the ABSOLUTE path unchanged when the worktree is outside the repo root. Repro: relPathOf('/Users/x/repo','/tmp/throwaway-wt') -> '/tmp/throwaway-wt', and it flows through worktreeView into lane.worktree.relPath and lane.key. The plan's own M6 probe ('git worktree add a throwaway detached worktree') is the trigger if the path is outside .worktrees/. Sibling-prefix ('/Users/x/repo2/wt') is handled correctly. Fix shape: outside-root -> a non-path marker within the existing whitelist (e.g. relPath = '<outside repo>' or basename) and a parse/ops test; implementer's call inside T4.
F3 OBSERVATION (merge seam, for the orchestrator): AS-28 (Lena, in review) adds a STATIC_FILES entry two lines below AS-99's '/lanes.js' entry and appends api tests directly above the AS-27 section where AS-99's loopFixture-based tests live; index.html hunks are head vs body. Expected to auto-merge, but whichever lands second gets a post-merge HOST run (expected 416 + 3 = 419) before its compose receipt is trusted.
F4 OBSERVATION (concurrency, not a defect): readLanes() reads .lattice/tasks/*.json live; a task file caught mid-rewrite by the lattice CLI is dropped by the tolerant readJson for that poll, so a worktree lane can flicker to unknown-task (and a task-only lane vanish) for <=1 lanes poll (5 s) with a frame pushed each way. Bounded and self-healing; noting it for AS-100's composer join.
F5 OBSERVATION: evaluate() runs <=13 synchronous git spawns per poll on the watcher's event loop (runSync). Tens of ms at WIP 3 on this repo; fine today, worth remembering if the poll cadence drops or the repo grows.
Seams checked clean: Dockerfile COPYs watch/ (server.js -> lib/lanes.js -> watcher import resolves in the image); watcher main() is argv[1]-guarded so the server import runs no watcher; defaultWriteState is tmp+rename so the server never sees a torn worktrees.json; readLoopFile's {error:'unparsable'} -> 'unreadable-snapshot'; parser handles locked/prunable/detached, summarizeStatus handles renames and quoted .lattice paths; classifyMerged returns null on any unknown fact; Escape chain is lanes(37) > org(36) > file > thread, task panel has no Escape handler (pre-existing) so both-open closes lanes first; lanesKey includes stale+reason so the 60 s flip pushes a frame without a file write.

SWEEP (floor check, AC-1..AC-14; 18 mutants on a scratch copy under scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/, site-anchored, applied asserted, restored from a pristine copy each time; test-file subsets run per mutant, cardinality shown as tests-run/failed):
AC-1 drop detached branch: 30/2 red {lanes-parse-detached, watcher-lanes-detached} (wider by 1, consistent). AC-1b throw on missing HEAD: 30/1 {lanes-parse-tolerant}.
AC-2 skip write when unchanged: 30/1 {watcher-lanes-generatedAt-advances}.
AC-3 throw on worktree-list failure: 30/1 {watcher-lanes-git-down}. AC-3b rethrow in outer catch: 30/2 {watcher-lanes-never-rejects, watcher-lanes-never-rejects-midway}.
AC-4 abort on first row status error: 30/1 {watcher-lanes-row-isolation}.
AC-5 drop --no-optional-locks: 30/1 {watcher-lanes-argv-pin}.
AC-6 drop first-parent term: 30/2 {lanes-merged-fresh-branch-is-not-merged, watcher-lanes-merged}.
AC-7a filter unjoined rows: 70/5 {lanes-compose-unknown-task-kept, lanes-compose-branch-name-fallback, lanes-compose-order, lanes-stale-boundary, lanes-compose-tolerant} (wider; every fixture with an unjoined row, consistent). AC-7b parse before link: 70/1 {lanes-compose-link-beats-name}.
AC-8 membership incl. blocked/needs_human: 70/1 {lanes-compose-task-only-membership}.
AC-9 flag on ahead===0: 70/1 {lanes-stale-reasons}.
AC-10 coalesce employee: 70/1 {lanes-employee-both-fields}.
AC-11a 2*LANES_STALE_MS: 70/2 {api-lanes-stale-boundary, lanes-stale-boundary}. AC-11b mtime in server.readLanes: 51/1 {api-lanes-stale-boundary}.
AC-12 push every poll: 10/1 {stream-lanes-change-only}.
AC-13 spread snapshot row: 70/2 {api-lanes-key-whitelist, lanes-compose-shape}.
AC-14 null payload -> '0': 11/1 {lanes-label-null-is-dash}.
Result: 14/14 criteria met with observed reds, 0 survivors; 2 findings outside the list (F1, F2).

HOST: branch 416/416 pass (node --test from .worktrees/AS-99/apps/chat); master baseline 367/367 (run, not computed); +49.
COMPOSE RECEIPT: VOID — docker is denied in this headless tick (AS-92); no 'Image … Built' line was obtained, no compose number is quoted. Merge precondition still owed from a live session or a tick with docker.
LIVE-PROBE LEDGER: performed — composer/label/parser/classifier edge probes via node against the worktree (above); server-planted-file and SSE behaviour via the api/stream tests' own ephemeral servers (AC-11, AC-12 red observed). Not performed — phone-width field count (no browser), kill-the-watcher stale caption at ~60 s and throwaway  on the host (would touch the real repo/watcher; forbidden and no docker), Escape with both modals open in a real DOM (verified statically only).
Owed before done: F1 fix + tests, F2 fix + test, then compose --build receipt.

Addendum to my review comment (qa-ruben): the F2 paragraph contains a block of git-worktree usage text that is NOT part of the finding. The comment body had a backticked phrase that my shell expanded before lattice received it; the command it ran was git worktree add with no arguments (prints usage, exit 128, no side effects — git worktree list verified unchanged). Read F2 as: relPathOf leaks the absolute host path for a worktree outside the repo root; the plan's own M6 throwaway-worktree probe is the trigger if that worktree lives outside .worktrees/. Verdict and every other line stand as written.

REVIEW CYCLE 1 → REWORK (orchestrator cto-owen, loop tick 6). Following Ruben's verdict: implementation-level rework. Findings appended to the plan under '## Review Cycle 1 Findings'. Marcus (fresh context, next tick) fixes F1 (git-error must render as a dash badge + 'Lane data unavailable' empty state, keyed off the reason, with label + api tests and mutants) and F2 (relPathOf must never emit an absolute path for an out-of-root worktree), on feat/AS-99-lane-view inside .worktrees/AS-99.
